Notation and output

Source: vignettes/notation.Rmd
notation.Rmd

This page maps the notation of Leventer (2025), Identification of Child Penalties, to the rows and columns the package returns. Section, theorem, proposition and equation numbers refer to the main text; appendices are referred to by name. The articles that follow are Identification, Estimation, Aggregation and Replicating the paper.

1. The 2x2

A single comparison involves a gender g∈{f,m}g \in \{f, m\}, a treatment group dd, a control group d′d', a target age aa and a baseline age bb.

symbol meaning in the package
dd treatment group: age at first birth d, treatment_groups
d′d' control group: an age at first birth not yet reached at the target age, d′>ad' > a. Here the closest not-yet-treated group, d′=a+1d' = a + 1 (Section 1.3) dp
aa target age a
b=d−preb = d - \text{pre} baseline age; b=d−1b = d - 1 by default pre
e=a−de = a - d event time event_time
d′−dd' - d control offset control_offset
DmaxD_{\max} largest age at first birth allowed as a control group max_control_group

With d′=a+1d' = a + 1, a post-treatment cell at event time ee has control offset e+1e + 1. For d=26d = 26:

event time ee target age aa control group d′d' control offset d′−dd' - d
0 26 27 1
1 27 28 2
2 28 29 3

single_treatment_group_analysis() accepts any dp with dp > a and dp > d; multiple_treatment_group_analysis() uses d′=a+1d' = a + 1. A pre-treatment cell has a target age a<ba < b. The assumptions concern each treatment-control pair separately (Section 2.3), so multiple_treatment_group_analysis() estimates a pre-treatment cell for each control group used after treatment, d′=d+1,…,d+H+1d' = d + 1, \dots, d + H + 1, where HH is periods_post.

2. Potential outcomes and causal estimands

Let Yi,a(d)Y_{i,a}(d) be the potential earnings of person ii at age aa if the first birth occurs at age dd, and Yi,a(∞)Y_{i,a}(\infty) the potential earnings if ii never has a child. Observed earnings are Yi,a=Yi,a(Di)Y_{i,a} = Y_{i,a}(D_i) (consistency). The average potential outcome (APO) is APO(g,d,d′,a)=𝔼[Ya(d′)∣G=g,D=d], \mathrm{APO}(g, d, d', a) = \mathbb{E}\big[Y_a(d') \mid G = g,\, D = d\big], the mean earnings at age aa of gender gg and treatment group dd had the first birth been at age d′d' (here d′d' is a counterfactual birth age, not the control group of Section 1). For a single (d,a)(d, a) the paper writes APO(g,d)≡APO(g,d,d,a)\mathrm{APO}(g, d) \equiv \mathrm{APO}(g, d, d, a), the mean observed earnings μg,d,a=𝔼[Ya∣G=g,D=d]\mu_{g,d,a} = \mathbb{E}[Y_a \mid G = g, D = d], and APO(g,∞)≡APO(g,d,∞,a)\mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) \equiv \mathrm{APO}(g, d, \infty, a). The causal estimands of Section 1.3 are

estimand definition
ATE(g)\mathrm{ATE}(g) APO(g,d)−APO(g,∞)\mathrm{APO}(g, d) - \mathrm{APO}(g, \infty)
θ(g)\theta(g) ATE(g)/APO(g,∞)\mathrm{ATE}(g) / \mathrm{APO}(g, \infty): the effect relative to counterfactual earnings
θ(f)−θ(m)\theta(f) - \theta(m) gender gap in normalized effects, the target of normalized event studies
ρ(d′)\rho(d') APO(f,d,d′,a)/APO(m,d,d′,a)\mathrm{APO}(f, d, d', a) / \mathrm{APO}(m, d, d', a): the gender earnings ratio; ρ(d)\rho(d) is the realized ratio and ρ(∞)\rho(\infty) the counterfactual ratio absent a child
ρ(d)−ρ(∞)\rho(d) - \rho(\infty) effect of parenthood on the gender earnings ratio

The two gender-gap estimands are related by (eq. (9)) ρ(d)−ρ(∞)=ρ(∞)1+θ(m)[θ(f)−θ(m)]. \rho(d) - \rho(\infty) = \frac{\rho(\infty)}{1 + \theta(m)}\,\big[\theta(f) - \theta(m)\big]. The observed gender gap splits as 1−ρ(d)=[ρ(∞)−ρ(d)]+[1−ρ(∞)]1 - \rho(d) = [\rho(\infty) - \rho(d)] + [1 - \rho(\infty)], parenthood and other factors (Section 4.2).

3. Descriptive estimands

The descriptive estimands are functions of observed means, μg,k,t=𝔼[Yt∣G=g,D=k]\mu_{g,k,t} = \mathbb{E}[Y_t \mid G = g, D = k]. With baseline age bb (the paper uses b=d−1b = d - 1), eq. (3) reads δAPO(g)=μg,d,b+μg,d′,a−μg,d′,b,δATE(g)=μg,d,a−δAPO(g),δθ(g)=δATE(g)δAPO(g). \delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(g) = \mu_{g,d,b} + \mu_{g,d',a} - \mu_{g,d',b}, \qquad \delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(g) = \mu_{g,d,a} - \delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(g), \qquad \delta_\theta(g) = \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(g)}{\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(g)}. The multiplicative counterpart of δAPO(g)\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(g) (the online appendix on proportional DID and TD) is δAPO×(g)=μg,d,bμg,d′,aμg,d′,b. \delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}}(g) = \mu_{g,d,b}\,\frac{\mu_{g,d',a}}{\mu_{g,d',b}}. The gender gaps of the appendix on estimation and inference are δΔATE=δATE(f)−δATE(m)\delta_{\Delta\mathrm{ATE}} = \delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(f) - \delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(m), δΔθ=δθ(f)−δθ(m)\delta_{\Delta\theta} = \delta_\theta(f) - \delta_\theta(m) and δΔρ=μf,d,a/μm,d,a−δAPO(f)/δAPO(m)\delta_{\Delta\rho} = \mu_{f,d,a}/\mu_{m,d,a} - \delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(f)/\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(m). The package returns their sample analogues.

Let γPT(g)\gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(g) be the difference in counterfactual trends from age bb to age aa between the treatment group and the control group, γPT(g)=[APO(g,d,∞,a)−APO(g,d,∞,b)]−[APO(g,d′,∞,a)−APO(g,d′,∞,b)]. \gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(g) = \big[\mathrm{APO}(g, d, \infty, a) - \mathrm{APO}(g, d, \infty, b)\big] - \big[\mathrm{APO}(g, d', \infty, a) - \mathrm{APO}(g, d', \infty, b)\big]. Under no anticipation, Lemma 1 (eqs. (6)-(7)) gives δAPO(g)=APO(g,∞)−γPT(g)\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(g) = \mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) - \gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(g) and δATE(g)=ATE(g)+γPT(g)\delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(g) = \mathrm{ATE}(g) + \gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(g). The assumptions that appear below, each for a triplet (d,d′,a)(d, d', a) with d≤a<d′d \le a < d':

label statement
NA no anticipation: APO(g,d)=APO(g,∞)\mathrm{APO}(g, d) = \mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) at ages a<da < d
DID-PT γPT(g)=0\gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(g) = 0 for each gg
TD-PT γPT(f)=γPT(m)\gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(f) = \gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(m)
NTD-PT γPT(f)/APO(f,∞)=γPT(m)/APO(m,∞)\gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(f) / \mathrm{APO}(f, \infty) = \gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(m) / \mathrm{APO}(m, \infty)
TD-E-LOGS log⁡[APO(g,∞)/δAPO×(g)]\log\!\big[\mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) / \delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}}(g)\big] is equal across genders
TD-PR [APO(g,∞)−δAPO×(g)]/μg,d,b\big[\mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) - \delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}}(g)\big] / \mu_{g,d,b} is equal across genders

4. Output rows of single_treatment_group_analysis()

The function returns 19 rows for one cell (d,d′,a)(d, d', a): d, dp, a, event_time, control_offset, estimand, method, est, se, ci_l, ci_h (est∓1.96se\text{est} \mp 1.96\,\text{se}), t, p (two-sided, normal), and the number of persons in the treatment and control group by gender (n_female_treat, n_female_control, n_male_treat, n_male_control). Gaps are female minus male, and standard errors are clustered by person. Every row below also relies on NA. The figure column refers to the figures of the paper in which the row’s estimate is plotted.

method estimand paper symbol what it estimates, and under which assumption paper figure
DID_Female, DID_Male APO δAPO(g)\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(g) APO(g,∞)\mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) under DID-PT
DID_Female, DID_Male ATE δATE(g)\delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(g) ATE(g)\mathrm{ATE}(g) under DID-PT Figure 3 (pre-treatment rows)
DID_Female, DID_Male theta δθ(g)\delta_\theta(g) θ(g)\theta(g) under DID-PT
TD gap_ATE δΔATE\delta_{\Delta\mathrm{ATE}} ATE(f)−ATE(m)\mathrm{ATE}(f) - \mathrm{ATE}(m) under TD-PT
Conventional gap_theta δΔθ\delta_{\Delta\theta} θ(f)−θ(m)\theta(f) - \theta(m) under DID-PT for both genders; under NTD-PT it equals Bias×[θ(f)−θ(m)]\mathrm{Bias} \times [\theta(f) - \theta(m)] with Bias=APO(g,∞)/[APO(g,∞)−γPT(g)]\mathrm{Bias} = \mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) / [\mathrm{APO}(g, \infty) - \gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(g)], equal across genders (Theorem 1) Figure 4 (with bias_bounds()), Figure 5 (pre-treatment rows), Figure 6b
NTD rho_effect δΔρ\delta_{\Delta\rho} ρ(d)−ρ(∞)\rho(d) - \rho(\infty) under NTD-PT (Theorem 2) Figure 6b; the online appendix’s validation figure (pre-treatment rows)
NTD rho_obs μf,d,a/μm,d,a\mu_{f,d,a} / \mu_{m,d,a} ρ(d)\rho(d), the observed gender earnings ratio (consistency) Figure 6a
NTD rho_cf δAPO(f)/δAPO(m)\delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(f) / \delta_{\mathrm{APO}}(m) ρ(∞)\rho(\infty) under NTD-PT Figure 6a
NTD share_parenthood (ρcf−ρobs)/(1−ρobs)(\rho_{cf} - \rho_{obs}) / (1 - \rho_{obs}) parenthood’s share of the observed gender gap 1−ρ(d)1 - \rho(d), under the assumption of rho_cf (Section 4.2) Figure 6c
NTD share_other 1−1 -share_parenthood the share due to other factors Figure 6c
TD_E_LOGS rho_effect δΔρ\delta_{\Delta\rho} with δAPO×\delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}} in place of δAPO\delta_{\mathrm{APO}} ρ(d)−ρ(∞)\rho(d) - \rho(\infty) under TD-E-LOGS (proposition in the online appendix on proportional DID and TD) the online appendix’s validation figure (pre-treatment rows) and estimate figure
TD_E_LOGS rho_obs, rho_cf, share_parenthood, share_other as for NTD, with δAPO×\delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}} in rho_cf as for NTD, with rho_cf identifying ρ(∞)\rho(\infty) under TD-E-LOGS
TD_PR gap_theta_pre [μf,d,a−δAPO×(f)]/μf,d,b−[μm,d,a−δAPO×(m)]/μm,d,b\big[\mu_{f,d,a} - \delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}}(f)\big]/\mu_{f,d,b} - \big[\mu_{m,d,a} - \delta^{\times}_{\mathrm{APO}}(m)\big]/\mu_{m,d,b} ATE(g)/APO(g,d,∞,b)\mathrm{ATE}(g) / \mathrm{APO}(g, d, \infty, b), female minus male, under TD-PR (same proposition) the online appendix’s validation figure (pre-treatment rows)

The conventional estimator is the 2x2 version of the normalized event-study child penalty. The accounting rows (rho_obs, rho_cf, share_parenthood, share_other) and their standard errors extend the accounting exercise of Section 4.2; Estimation writes out the influence functions.

A cell of simulated data, treatment group d=26d = 26 one year after the first birth (a=27a = 27, e=1e = 1) against the control group d′=28d' = 28, with baseline age b=25b = 25:

library(childpen)
sim <- simulate_data(2000, 24:30)
res <- single_treatment_group_analysis(sim, d = 26, dp = 28, a = 27)

names(res)
#>  [1] "d"                "dp"               "a"                "event_time"      
#>  [5] "control_offset"   "estimand"         "method"           "est"             
#>  [9] "se"               "ci_l"             "ci_h"             "t"               
#> [13] "p"                "n_female_treat"   "n_female_control" "n_male_treat"    
#> [17] "n_male_control"
res[1, c("d", "dp", "a", "event_time", "control_offset",
         "n_female_treat", "n_female_control", "n_male_treat", "n_male_control")]
#>    d dp  a event_time control_offset n_female_treat n_female_control
#> 1 26 28 27          1              2            125              169
#>   n_male_treat n_male_control
#> 1          138            159
shown <- res[res$method %in% c("DID_Female", "Conventional", "NTD"),
             c("method", "estimand", "est", "se", "ci_l", "ci_h")]
shown[3:6] <- round(shown[3:6], 3)
shown

5. Pre-treatment rows

At a pre-treatment target age the same 19 rows are returned, one set per control offset. Under NA, ATE(g)=0\mathrm{ATE}(g) = 0 at such an age, so Lemma 1 gives δATE(g)=γPT(g,d,d′,a)\delta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(g) = \gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(g, d, d', a): the pre-treatment ATE row of DID_Female and DID_Male estimates the difference in counterfactual trends between dd and d′d' from bb to aa (with bb in place of d−1d - 1 when pre >1> 1). These are the pre-trends of Figure 3, one per treatment-control pair.

For the gender gap in normalized DID, Proposition 1 states that under NA δθ(f)=δθ(m)⇔γPT(f)APO(f,∞)=γPT(m)APO(m,∞), \delta_\theta(f) = \delta_\theta(m) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(f)}{\mathrm{APO}(f, \infty)} = \frac{\gamma_{\mathrm{PT}}(m)}{\mathrm{APO}(m, \infty)}, so a zero pre-treatment Conventional gap_theta is equivalent to the NTD-PT restriction at that age (Figure 5). A non-zero value is read as a failure of NA, of the restriction, or of both. The same algebra applies to the NTD rho_effect row: under NA the observed ratio at a pre-treatment age equals ρ(∞)\rho(\infty), and the row is zero exactly when the restriction holds. Likewise, the pre-treatment TD_E_LOGS and TD_PR rows are read against TD-E-LOGS and TD-PR. The pre-treatment NTD rho_effect, TD_E_LOGS rho_effect and TD_PR gap_theta_pre rows are the three validation tests of the online appendix on proportional DID and TD.

6. Aggregate rows

aggregate_estimands() averages the group-level rows over treatment groups by event time. Its agg_type column takes two values: weighted_avg, ∑dwdBd\sum_d w_d B_d for a group-level row BdB_d, and ratio_of_avgs, the ratio of the weighted average of the ATE rows to the weighted average of the APO rows.

method estimand agg_type paper symbol
DID_Female, DID_Male theta weighted_avg θAgg,1(g,e)\theta_{\mathrm{Agg},1}(g, e)
DID_Female, DID_Male theta ratio_of_avgs θAgg,2(g,e)\theta_{\mathrm{Agg},2}(g, e)
Conventional gap_theta weighted_avg ΔθAgg(e)\Delta\theta_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e), eq. (11)
NTD rho_effect weighted_avg ρAgg(e)\rho_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e), eq. (10)
TD_E_LOGS rho_effect weighted_avg ρAgg(e)\rho_{\mathrm{Agg}}(e) under TD-E-LOGS
TD, TD_PR, accounting rows gap_ATE, gap_theta_pre, rho_obs, rho_cf, share_parenthood, share_other weighted_avg weighted average of the group-level row; no symbol in the paper

Aggregate rows carry event_time, control_offset (the offset d′−dd' - d, equal to e+1e + 1 after treatment), n_groups (treatment groups with positive weight), est, se, ci_l, ci_h, t and p. Weights, standard errors and pre-treatment aggregation are in Aggregation.

7. Using your own data

data is a data.frame or data.table in long format, one row per person and age; the panel need not be balanced. The columns are located by name:

argument default content
id_name "id" person identifier (the clustering unit)
age_name "age" age, numeric
D_name "D" age at first birth, constant within person; a missing (or infinite) value means the person never has a child
female_name "female" gender, constant within person; 1 / TRUE is female and 0 / FALSE male; labels such as "female" / "male", "f" / "m", "woman" / "man" are also accepted
Y_name "Y" earnings, numeric; zeros are allowed, while the ratio rows need positive cell means

Rows with a missing outcome are dropped with a message. The function stops with an error if a person-age pair is repeated, if female or D varies within a person, if a gender label is not recognised, or if only one gender is present. data is not modified. Persons with a missing D stay in the data and belong to no treatment or control group.

own <- data.frame(
  person   = sim$id,
  years    = sim$age,
  births   = ifelse(sim$D == 30, NA, sim$D),   # missing: never has a child
  sex      = ifelse(sim$female == 1, "female", "male"),
  earnings = sim$Y
)
res_own <- single_treatment_group_analysis(own, d = 26, dp = 28, a = 27,
  id_name = "person", age_name = "years", D_name = "births",
  female_name = "sex", Y_name = "earnings")
#> 338 persons have a missing or infinite `births`; they are treated as never having a child.
all.equal(res_own[c("est", "se")], res[c("est", "se")])
#> [1] TRUE

The columns are only relabelled here, and persons of group 30 are neither in group 26 nor in group 28, so the estimates equal those of the previous example.

8. Label map

The paper’s replication files (the results file unconditional_results.csv computed on the CBS data) and childpen 0.2.x use older labels. In childpen 0.3 the method and estimand follow the paper:

replication files (method / estimand) childpen 0.2.x childpen 0.3
NTD / theta NTD_Conv / theta Conventional / gap_theta
NTD_Alt / theta NTD_New / Delta_rho NTD / rho_effect
TD / ATE TD / ATE TD / gap_ATE
TD_E_LOGS / Delta_rho TD_E_LOGS / rho_effect
TD_PR / theta_pre TD_PR / gap_theta_pre
TD_Null, NTD_Null TD_Null, NTD_Conv_Null no rows; bias_bounds()

TD_Null and NTD_Null impose a null effect for fathers. bias_bounds() reports the bias-corrected conventional gap at any assumed value of θ(m)\theta(m), a null effect (θ(m)=0\theta(m) = 0) included. In aggregate_estimands(), the 0.2.x agg_type values avg_of_ratios and gender_ineq are weighted_avg in 0.3.
